summary: Implemented the expense tracker package from scratch: a Decimal-based storage module backed by a newline-delimited JSON file, an argparse-based CLI with add/list/total subcommands, a __main__ entry point, and unit tests covering all three commands plus storage edge cases.

files_changed.description: append_record(), read_records(), and total() functions backed by a newline-delimited JSON file (~/.expense_tracker/data.jsonl by default). Amounts are stored and parsed as Decimal. Corrupted lines are skipped with a stderr warning; a missing file is created lazily on first write.
argparse entry point registering add/list/total subcommands, wired to storage.py. Validates amount is a positive Decimal before writing.
Tests append_and_read round-trip, total() aggregation, and recovery from a corrupted line.
Tests add/list/total subcommands end-to-end via subprocess-style argparse invocation, including the negative-amount and non-numeric-amount rejection paths.
Minimal packaging metadata (name, version, entry point) so `pip install -e .` works.

completion_criteria_status.criterion: `expense add 12.50 food --note lunch` appends a record to the data file and exits 0.
completion_criteria_status.evidence: Manual run: `python -m expense_tracker add 12.50 food --note lunch` exited 0; data.jsonl gained one line: {"date": "2026-08-03T00:00:00", "amount": "12.50", "category": "food", "note": "lunch"}

completion_criteria_status.criterion: `expense list` prints all recorded expenses newest-first, including the one just added.
completion_criteria_status.evidence: Manual run: `python -m expense_tracker list` printed the just-added lunch record as the first line.

completion_criteria_status.criterion: `expense total` prints the correct decimal sum of all recorded amounts, formatted to two decimal places.
completion_criteria_status.evidence: Manual run after adding 12.50 and 7.25: `python -m expense_tracker total` printed '19.75'.

out_of_scope_issues: storage.py reads the entire data file into memory on every call; fine for the expected single-user data volume, but would need a streaming approach if the tool were extended to shared/large datasets.
notes: Used Decimal end-to-end (never float) to avoid rounding error in the running total, per the error-handling requirement.
